text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government will ask the Aid-to-Pakistan consortium, meeting in Paris on April 22 and 23, for a $2.3 billion loan for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
- Pakistan has neither agreed to "freeze" the Jammu and Kashmir issue with India nor place it "on the back burner," a foreign office spokesman said.
- In the biggest bank robbery of the year committed in Karachi, bandits looted over 5.6 million rupees ($136,000) from a branch of the private Muslim Commercial Bank.
- The wheat consignments ready to be transported to Karachi from another district of the Sindh province have been diverted to Punjab province to meet wheat shortages there.
- Two people were wounded when guards at a flour mill opened fire on an angry mob that had gathered there to buy flour.

- The Karachi police have registered a case against former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, ex-interior minister Naseerullah Babar and former Sindh province chief minister Syed Abdullah Shah for their alleged role in the murder of the brother-in-law of the exiled leader of ethnic Mohajir National Movement, Altaf Hussain in December 1995.
- Indian and Pakistani troops shelled each other's positions along the line of control in the disputed territory of Kashmir.

- The annual plan for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) is expected to set a gross domestic product growth target of seven percent led by industrial growth at 8.9 percent, export growth of 15 percent, rate of inflation at nine percent, current account deficit of 5.2 percent of GDP and an ambitious investment target of 633.2 billion rupees.
- The federal government has decided to release one billion rupees for import of sugar from the international market, sources said.
- Communications Minister, Azam Hoti has ruled out the privatisation of the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd unless the company fetches reasonable price.
- The state-run Water and Power Development Authority is planning to launch Energy Bonds worth four billion rupees to mobilise long-term funds for its expansion and meet its current obligations.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) has approved Jardine Fleming Pakistan's application for a seat on the KSE.
